Newcombe Hybrid Score CI for a difference of two proportions

Source: R/newcombes_hs.r
ks_newcombe_hs.Rd

Computes a confidence interval for \(p_1 - p_2\) using Newcombe's Hybrid Score method (Newcombe, 1998, Method 10). Each group's proportion is first bounded by its Wilson score interval, and the two intervals are then combined to yield the CI for the difference.

Usage

ks_newcombe_hs(x1, n1, x2, n2, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

x1

Integer vector of event counts for group 1 (\(\ge 0\)).

n1

Integer vector of sample sizes for group 1 (\(> 0\)).

x2

Integer vector of event counts for group 2 (\(\ge 0\)).

n2

Integer vector of sample sizes for group 2 (\(> 0\)).

alpha

Significance level; scalar in \((0,1)\). Defaults to 0.05 (95% CI).

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per input pair and three columns:

delta

Observed difference \(\hat p_1 - \hat p_2\).

lcl

Lower confidence limit.

ucl

Upper confidence limit.

Details

Algorithm (Newcombe, 1998):

  1. Compute the Wilson score CI \([l_i,\, u_i]\) for each group at level \(1-\alpha\): $$l_i,\, u_i = \frac{2x_i + z^2 \mp z\sqrt{z^2 + 4x_i(n_i-x_i)/n_i}}{2(n_i + z^2)}$$

  2. Form the CI for \(\delta = p_1 - p_2\): $$\mathrm{LCL} = \hat\delta - \sqrt{(p_1-l_1)^2 + (u_2-p_2)^2}$$ $$\mathrm{UCL} = \hat\delta + \sqrt{(u_1-p_1)^2 + (p_2-l_2)^2}$$

The function is vectorised: if vectors of length \(k\) are supplied, each corresponding tuple \((x_{1i}, n_{1i}, x_{2i}, n_{2i})\) is processed independently and the result is a \(k \times 3\) matrix.

References

Newcombe, R. G. (1998). Interval estimation for the difference between independent proportions: comparison of eleven methods. Statistics in Medicine, 17(8), 873–890. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19980430)17:8<873::AID-SIM779>3.0.CO;2-I

See also

ks_newcombe_hs_strata, ks_eairdiff_mn

Examples

## Single comparison
ks_newcombe_hs(36L, 54L, 41L, 56L, alpha = 0.10)
#>            delta        lcl       ucl
#> [1,] -0.06547619 -0.2054461 0.0773548

## Zero events in one group
ks_newcombe_hs(0L, 50L, 10L, 50L)
#>      delta        lcl         ucl
#> [1,]  -0.2 -0.3303711 -0.08705014

## Vectorised: three comparisons at once
ks_newcombe_hs(
  x1 = c(36L, 38L, 3L),
  n1 = c(54L, 57L, 86L),
  x2 = c(41L, 42L, 3L),
  n2 = c(56L, 57L, 93L),
  alpha = 0.10
)
#>             delta         lcl        ucl
#> [1,] -0.065476190 -0.20544613 0.07735480
#> [2,] -0.070175439 -0.20690888 0.07020393
#> [3,]  0.002625656 -0.04764532 0.05550182
